body:
I can add some explanatory comment. I will not revert it to the `if-elif-else` switches.
I will wait with this update until we have resolved the other discussion points above.

The doublet OH was included since its not a closed shell molecule to start with unlike LiH. Its a bit bigger and hence the bit slower. It was to make sure we were doing things right with either type of molecule across the different methods - it was originally called test driver methods. How long does it take to run that you consider it slow? If anything I could support perhaps putting some of them oh_uhf/oh_rohf (same for lih_uhf/rohf/rhf) as slow where they test the same thing but with a different mapping to thin things down. Arguably if it works for one mapping it should be good for the others - if it does not its more likely the mapper is broke than the driver. Having said that I am not sure we have mapping tests with such coverage of open shell molecules elsewhere.

body: I guess in my mind it makes the code 'brittle' in that refactoring an enum, should we ever want to change any name, this detection here would break. Listing the set and simply saying `if x in [A, B, C]` works and if we refactor C to D that code should get changed by the refactor whereas some check on "C" would not.

With a switch, that was calling to the methods directly, tooling can check and show issues. Here if things change any tooling (lint, IDEs) etc are unlikely to spot any issue. In that regard its easier/simpler to see things too as one is coding. Here of course unit tests should run through all the possibilities and would ensure it continues to work.
